Nov 24 : Elon Musk's two public companies have appointed five directors, three from Tesla and two from SpaceX, to guide two special committees handling merger negotiations, The Financial Times reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.  Those directors are Roelof Botha and Randy Glein from SpaceX and Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung from Tesla, the report said.  Reuters could not immediately verify the report. SpaceX and Tesla did no immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

Source: Reuters

FAST

NEW DELHI: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from more than two years of exile in India on Dec 16, the anniversary of the end of her country's 1971 liberation war with Pakistan, her spokesperson told Reuters on Tuesday (Nov 24). It is the first time Hasina has set a specific date for her return, potentially raising political and legal tensions in a country where her party is banned and where violence has risen since she sought a new passport and other documents earlier this month. In addition to seeking the paperwork, cancelled months after she fled to Delhi following a deadly uprising against her, Hasina has urged the Bangladeshi government to arrange her return on flag carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines. "Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on Aug 5, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," the spokesperson, Syed Mozammel Ali, said in a statement. "Having exiled her contrary to the Constitution under such circumstances, it is now the responsibility of the government to make possible her return to Bangladesh on Victory Day on Dec 16th." A Bangladeshi government spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A Bangladeshi minister told Reuters on Sunday that Hasina, who faces a death sentence, would be arrested and jailed on return , and that there had been no official discussions with India about sending an aircraft to bring her back. The United Nations has said as many as 1,400 people were killed during the unrest that forced her out of power. Bangladesh's war crimes court sentenced her to death in November last year in her absence for ordering a deadly crackdown on the student-led uprising, though she has denied the charges from exile.

JAKARTA: Indonesian police have charged a former police chief with treason after an investigation into alleged illegal wiretapping widened to activities authorities claim were aimed at undermining public trust in President Prabowo Subianto's government, a senior official said. The charges followed accusations that officials were involved in the widespread and unauthorised wiretapping of phones belonging to Prabowo as well as government officials, activists and journalists.  Six officials have now been named as suspects, the chief of the police's criminal investigation unit, Asep Safrudin, said late on Monday (Nov 23), including former police chief  Listyo Sigit Prabowo , known as a political ally of Prabowo's predecessor Joko Widodo. He is unrelated to President Prabowo. "The suspects allegedly agreed to, prepared for, and initiated treason with the motive of maintaining the position of the police chief ... by lowering the people's trust in the government of President Prabowo Subianto," Asep said.

Arrested earlier this month, Listyo allegedly ordered and received wiretap reports from the other suspects, Asep said. Asep said authorities also seized 20 "One Piece" flags, symbols that have appeared at anti-government demonstrations in Indonesia. They raided 14 locations, Asep added. A flag containing "One Piece" character Monkey D Luffy was unfurled by authorities during the press conference, although the text said "One Peace", according to a video from news outlet Kompas. Asep said authorities are probing whether the suspects were involved in "exploiting" the mass demonstrations. The other suspects, all of whom Asep referred to by their initials, are alleged to have committed acts such as mobilising the demonstrations and creating social media content that disparaged the police, Asep said. Two of the suspects were dishonourably discharged from the police in separate ethics hearings earlier this month. Listyo will be the subject of an ethics hearing on Thursday, police spokesperson Trunoyudo Wisnu Andiko said on Tuesday. Reuters could not immediately contact the suspects. Presidential spokesperson Prasetyo Hadi also did not immediately respond to a request for comment.  The allegations against Listyo have fuelled speculation about tensions between Prabowo and his predecessor Widodo.

Source: Reuters/aj

FAST

Nov 24 : Oil prices eased on Tuesday, hovering near a three-month low on concern over rising crude supply and a potential market surplus, while risk to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz persisted. Brent crude futures fell 40 cents, or 0.45 per cent, to $88.97 a barrel by 0147 GMT after posting their lowest close since August 31 on Monday. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 23 cents, or 0.29 per cent, to $79.94 a barrel, after hitting their lowest level since August 26 earlier in the session. Prices drew support from shipping risk in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said three "violating" oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the strait on Monday, Iran's Press TV reported. The United States is investigating whether Iran was involved in cyberattacks on as many as 50 energy tankers, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials and others familiar with the matter.

Better supply has weighed on prices, though analysts said the market remained fragile. "Despite some improvement in inventories and product availability, the oil market remains under severe strain," said Daniel Hynes, senior commodity strategist at ANZ, in a client note. "Oil prices, time spreads, refining margins and investor positioning increasingly suggest the market expects conditions to normalise. Yet logistics remain constrained and inventory buffers are thin. The oil system therefore appears to be moving from acute scarcity towards persistent vulnerability, rather than returning to normal," Hynes said. Supply is also recovering in Libya. The country's Sharara oil pipeline has reopened, and oil has begun to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya, the chairperson of the National Oil Corporation told Reuters on Monday. Global observed liquids inventory rose 52 million barrels in October, implying an oversupply of 1.7 million barrels each day, Deutsche Bank said in a research note. Evidence is accumulating that the global market is rebalancing and turning into surplus, although setbacks could delay progress, the bank said. US crude oil and product inventories likely rose last week, a preliminary Reuters poll showed.

Source: Reuters
